data.statement: Fix Speech Blocks narrator-plus-character generation so chunks with non-spoken quoted words inside narration do not reject otherwise valid atomic-unit speaker assignments and collapse multi-character chunks such as DuneMessiah chunk-0004 into one narrator fallback block.

acceptance: A focused red-before-green test proves quoted narrator words like Not 'our' Emperor / 'Your' Emperor remain narration and no longer force atomic-unit fallback, while existing dialogue-attribution merge rejection tests remain green.
assumptions: Short quoted words embedded in narrator prose without dialogue punctuation or local speech attribution are non-spoken emphasis/mention text and should remain narration.
data.reason: The failure mode is localized to deterministic atomic-unit classification and validation, has existing linked requirements, and the user approved continuing without another prompt until before delivery.
scope: In scope: focused regression tests for quoted words inside narration, atomic quote classification changes, relevant Speech Blocks/Text Pipeline component documentation, and focused validation. Out of scope: changing LLM prompts broadly, regenerating DuneMessiah runtime artifacts, delivery packaging, pushing, PR creation, or implementing streaming/model progress changes.
data.source: user runtime defect report and DuneMessiah chunk-0004 log analysis
data.understanding: Speech Blocks narrator-and-character generation currently rejects otherwise valid multi-character atomic-unit speaker assignments when deterministic atomic parsing labels non-spoken quoted words inside narrator prose as dialogue. The rejected response falls back to one giant narrator block, as seen in DuneMessiah chunk-0004. The fix should keep real dialogue and attribution strict while treating narrator emphasis/mention quotes inside prose as narration so valid model selections are accepted.
